page: Microsoft Azure E8a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at 3.35 GHz. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Local scratch storage is bundled as a 215 GB SSD, and no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark outcomes show midrange general compute capabilities alongside distinct memory-intensive limitations. In general computing suites, the instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1397.0 and a multi-core score of 5142.0, while PassMark CPU yields 10122.73, all placing in the middle 50% tier. However, sustained synthetic stress testing reflects lower execution throughput, with stress-ng single-core in the bottom 10% (769.79) and multi-core in the bottom 25% (3083.05). Uncached memory bandwidth tests similarly register lower throughput, logging 27.0 GB/sec for large-block reads and 13.49 GB/sec for writes (bottom 10%), despite robust small-block cached read performance of 404.34 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure perspective, the high RAM-to-core allocation provides resource efficiency for workloads that depend primarily on memory capacity rather than raw compute speed or high memory bandwidth. In operational testing, the instance maintains steady middle-tier throughput for caching engines, achieving 7.1 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations also register in the middle 50% tier at 2710.41. The E8a_v4 is an appropriate hardware fit for relational databases, Redis or Memcached instances, enterprise application runtimes, and intermediate ETL pipelines that require large active memory spaces.
description: Microsoft Azure E8a_v4 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.35 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs over 4 physical cores, paired with 64.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio. Ephemeral local storage is provided via a bundled 215 GB SSD, and it contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks place the system in the middle 50% category for Geekbench (multi-core score of 5142.0) and PassMark CPU (10122.73), though sustained stress-ng compute tests and large-block uncached memory write operations fall into the lower performance brackets. The instance yields stable throughput for Redis caching (7.1 million SET ops/sec) and static web serving (9.9 GB/sec). It is targeted at memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caches, enterprise databases, and ETL staging environments.
